related_questions.question: How to qualify for free legal aid in Florida?
related_questions.snippet: Generally, you will be eligible if your income does not exceed 125% of the Federal Poverty Income Guidelines. In some counties and in some cases, domestic violence and elderly clients may not be subject to the income guidelines.
related_questions.title: Eligibility for Assistance - Community Legal Services

related_questions.question: What is the income limit for legal aid in Florida?

text_blocks.snippet: In Florida, legal aid programs generally serve individuals with incomes at or below 125% of the federal poverty guidelines. For example, in 2021, a single individual earning $16,100 or less, or a family of four with an income below $33,125, would typically qualify. However, specific asset limits may also apply, and these vary between different legal aid programs.

list.title: 125% of Federal Poverty Guidelines:
list.snippet: This is the standard income threshold used by many legal aid programs in Florida.

list.title: Varying Asset Limits:
list.snippet: Legal aid programs also consider assets like savings, property, and other financial resources when determining eligibility.

list.title: Specific Program Guidelines:
list.snippet: Each legal aid program may have its own specific income and asset limits, so it's essential to check with the individual program for their exact requirements, according to Legal Services Corporation (LSC).

list.title: Submit an Application:
list.snippet: Individuals seeking legal aid will need to submit an application, which typically requires providing detailed financial information.

list.title: Provide Financial Documentation:
list.snippet: Applicants may need to submit proof of income (e.g., pay stubs, tax returns) and documentation of their assets.

list.title: Contact a Local Provider:
list.snippet: The best way to determine eligibility and apply is to contact a legal aid organization in your area.

list.title: Single Individual:
list.snippet: An individual earning at or below $16,100 annually in 2021 may be eligible for assistance.

list.title: Family of Four:
list.snippet: A family of four with an income at or below $33,125 annually in 2021 may also qualify.

text_blocks.snippet: To find out if you qualify for free legal aid in Florida, it's best to contact a local legal aid provider or the Legal Services Corporation (LSC).
